newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares close lower in correction.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares close lower in correction.

text.p: Israeli shares closed broadly lower on Wednesday in what traders said was a correction after recent sharp gains, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of top 100 shares fell 1.12 percent, or 3.02 points, to 267.55 on heavy all-share turnover of 207 million shekels against 233 million shekels on Tuesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 1.26 percent lower at 274.24.

"The market had gained seven percent from the beginning of the week and a technical correction had to come. I believe that the trigger for today's decline was the Deri story," said a trader at Tachlit Investments.

Aryeh Deri, Shas party leader and a key political figure, was alleged in newspaper reports published on Wednesday morning to have promoted the appointment of a candidate for attorney-general in exchange for his support for the deal to handover most of Hebron to the PLO.
The allegations came in a letter from Deri's attorney leaked to the press. Deri denied the allegations as a "complete lie".

"This was only the trigger, but investors were looking for a reason to take profits. This is not the beginning of a negative trend it's only a normal consolidation that might continue a few days," the Tachlit trader said. "I believe that the Mishtanim will not fall below 260."
Other traders said the police investigation had no impact on trading. "People are looking for reasons but it's only a technical correction," said another trader.
"In the short-run the market could be very volatile and the fact that we did not see a real correction in the Karam index (of small capitalisation stocks) is very worrying," the trader said.
"New money keeps coming into the mutual funds that specialise in Karam stocks. This is not healthy -- the small caps need to slow down," he added.

Dead Sea Bromine led gains on the Maof with a 3.25 percent rise to 2,250 agorot. Traders said the share rose after parent Israel Chemicals won a $10 million order for 100,000 tonnes of potash from China's Sinochem, which will be filled by Dead Sea.
Israel Chemicals, the most active share, rose 2.0 percent to 407 agorot on turnover of 12.2 million shekels.

Other active shares included Bank Leumi, which gained 1.25 percent to 567 agorot on volume of 12 million shekels, and Delek Israel Fuel Corp, which rose 2.0 percent to 10,880 agorot on turnover of 8.2 million shekels.
